newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss franc drifts lower in dollar-led trade.
newsitem.headline: Swiss franc drifts lower in dollar-led trade.

text.p: 1430 GMT - The Swiss franc ended lower, taking a cue from the strong dollar, although the dollar closed in Zurich off day's highs.
One Swiss technical analyst described dollar business as "range trading at higher levels."

Aurel David at Bank Julius Baer saw further opportunity for dollar/Swiss gains. A drop to 1.4695 francs to the downside presenting a buying opportunity. He would reverse long positions at 1.4630 francs, which may signal a move to 1.4550.
Overall he remained bullish. A break of 1.4815 francs to the upside could lead to a test of 1.4885 francs.
Further to the upside, 1.5050 was seen possible in the next few weeks.
In the U.S., declines in U.S. Treasury bonds may have triggered some late European profit-taking in dollars.

Adam Beaudin, analyst at CS, said participants were likely also nervous when the dollar got up near 1.72 marks, while 1.4790 francs was seen as resistance. European trade was fairly volatile. The dollar hit a morning high of 1.4780 francs, after testing lows early in the day near 1.4680.
In Switzerland, the jobless rate was reported down slightly in March at 5.6 percent versus 5.7 percent in February.
* Dollar ends at 1.4702/4708 Swiss francs, above Monday's close of 1.4677/4683. The close was lower than the opening of 1.4710/20 francs.
* Mark ends higher at 85.94/95 Swiss centimes versus 85.86/87 centimes on Monday. The opening on Tuesday was 85.84/86.
